fields.title: Protein degradation targets in hippocampus and retrosplenial cortex of the aged brain
fields.description: This project examined changes in degradation-specific K48 polyubiquitination in the hippocampus across the lifespan and during memory formation in old age in rats.
fields.sample_protocol: Samples were the dorsal CA1 region of the hippocampus or retrosplenial cortex tissue dissected from male and female (CA1 only) Fischer F344 rats that were 3-, 12-, or 23-24 months old. Additional 24-month old male rats were trained to contextual fear conditioning, euthanized 1 hour later and the dorsal CA1 region of the hippocampus collected; for these naïve 24-month old animals were the baseline control. Samples were homogenized in denaturing lysis buffer (0.05% SDS) with 70mM NEM, briefly centrifuged and supernatant collected. Normalized samples were mixed with a K48 polyubiquitin-specific Tandem Ubiquitin Binding Entity (TUBE; Life Sensors) bound to magnetic streptavidin beads and incubated at 4C. Samples were then washed and protein eluted in 1x sample buffer at 95C, 800 rpm for 5 minutes. Samples were then washed and protein eluted in 1x sample buffer at 95C, 800 rpm for 5 minutes. Samples were processed utilizing S-Trap micro columns (Protofi) and trypsin. Recovered peptides were analyzed via LC-ESI-MS/MS on an Orbitrap Fusion Lumos Tribid instrument (Thermo) running each sample in duplicate.
fields.reference_titles: Dysregulation of baseline and learning-dependent protein degradation in the aged hippocampus
